claims.text: In-situ substrate preheating at approximately 400 °C combined with real-time laser power modulation during SLM will reduce residual thermal stresses in AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
The combined intervention will improve the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi miniature components relative to conventional high-thermal-load SLM.
The AlCrFeNiSi feedstock has particle size distribution and purity typical for SLM processing.
The proposed intervention consists of substrate preheating near 400 °C under an inert atmosphere and real-time laser power modulation.
A substrate-preheating window of 200–600 °C, optimized near 400 °C, is applicable to SLM processing of AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
An argon atmosphere with low oxygen is suitable for the proposed SLM process.
Residual stress can be evaluated by X-ray diffraction and mechanical properties by nanoindentation and microhardness testing.
Substrate preheating reduces thermal gradients and rapid cooling during layer deposition.
Reduced thermal gradients produce a more uniform, fine-grained microstructure.
Reduced thermal gradients and moderated cooling lower contraction-induced internal residual stresses.
Real-time laser power modulation ensures optimized energy deposition.
Coordinated preheating and laser-power modulation moderate solidification and reduce defect formation.
The intervention will yield significantly lower residual stresses, increased hardness, and a more uniform microstructure than conventional high-thermal-load SLM.
SLM without substrate preheating causes rapid cooling, high thermal gradients, increased residual stress, and degraded mechanical properties.
The proposed 200–600 °C process window is limited to miniature AlCrFeNiSi geometries and may not transfer to other sizes, geometries, or alloy systems.
Powder variation and machine-specific parameters may affect the process outcomes.
Failure to obtain both a statistically significant mechanical-property improvement and a residual-stress reduction relative to an unpreheated control would falsify the hypothesis.
